World News: China and Russia have kicked off their annual Joint Sea-2025 naval exercises in the Sea of Japan just as India prepares to hold its first joint drills with the Philippines in the South China Sea.

China & Russia: The three-day drills, launched near the Russian port of Vladivostok, include joint anti-submarine warfare, air and missile defense, and live-fire naval combat. Among the participating vessels are China’s guided-missile destroyers Shaoxing and Urumqi, the rescue ship Xihu, and Russia’s Admiral Tributs, a large anti-submarine ship, along with the corvette Rezky and the submarine support ship Igor Belousov. Subs are also involved in the drills. 

According to China’s Ministry of National Defense, the drills are designed to “further deepen the comprehensive strategic partnership” between the two countries and are not aimed at any third party. The Chinese military added that the exercises are “unrelated to the current international and regional situations,” a message intended to downplay rising concerns from neighboring countries.

This comes as many Western countries, including Japan, have raised concerns about the growing military ties between China and Russia. Japan, in particular, has called the drills near its waters a “serious security concern.”

India & Philippines: Coincidentally, India and the Philippines are preparing to conduct their first joint naval exercises in the South China Sea. The drills will include an Indian guided-missile destroyer, an anti-submarine warfare corvette, and a surveillance ship, along with Philippine vessels. 

The Philippines, which has beef with China over disputed territorial waters, has continued ramping up joint drills with many Western countries (the US, Australia, Japan, France, and Canada) amid tensions in the region. India also has issues with China, including territorial disputes 

Chinese state media have downplayed the drills, calling India’s move “gesture politics” and saying it would likely lack “real combat significance.”

No comment from India yet.
